turns.input: Can Playback work with our setup? We have an iPad and want to send the tracks wirelessly to a Bluetooth sound system for Sunday worship.
turns.reply:
Absolutely, let me pull that up. One moment please.

Bluetooth isn’t one of Playback’s documented audio-output options, so I can’t confirm it as a reliable Sunday setup. Playback supports a wired headphone connection, a class-compliant USB audio interface, or networked audio; are you hoping to send just the tracks to the sound system, or also keep click and guide separate?

results.title: How to Use Playback with Your Sound System
results.summary: Three documented ways to get audio out of Playback: the built-in headphone port with Auto-Pan (2 channels: click/guide left, tracks right), a USB audio interface (up to 32 outputs, grouped into mono or stereo buses), and networked audio such as Dante or SoundGrid (iPad/iPhone limited to two channels; macOS can route up to 32 via Dante Virtual Soundcard). Bluetooth, subscription tiers, and menu paths are not covered here.

steps.text: Option 1 - headphone port: Auto-Pan is on by default. Use a 1/8" TRS to dual 1/4" TS cable, a stereo DI (or two mono DIs) to convert to XLR, then XLR to the stage box. Devices without a headphone jack can use a Lightning-to-3.5mm or USB-C-to-3.5mm adapter. Left channel feeds in-ears (click/guide); right feeds the house mix.

Option 2 - USB audio interface: up to 32 outputs via a supported class-compliant interface. Lightning devices need an Apple Lightning Digital AV Adapter; USB-C devices need an Apple USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter. Add a powered USB hub if the interface is bus-powered. Outputs are grouped into custom buses, mono or stereo.

Option 3 - networked audio (Dante, SoundGrid): connect the Playback device to a network running that protocol. iPad and iPhone support only two channels over networked audio; macOS apps like Dante Virtual Soundcard can route up to 32 channels.
Use an in-ear monitoring solution so click and guide are not heard by the congregation. Accompaniment tracks do not include click and guide.

results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues
results.summary: Focuses on dropouts and disconnections in live setups. Four checks: device/OS/app up to date, iOS performance (RAM, background apps), the USB connection (named as the most common cause in MultiOut setups), and the audio connection (Auto Pan splitter cable, class-compliant interfaces). The article does not cover no-sound, output selection, Bluetooth, sample rate, or mono/stereo settings.

steps.text: Check the device is supported (supported devices list for iOS, iPadOS, macOS). On the oldest supported iOS generation, Multi-Outs and MIDI Cue editing are limited.
Confirm the OS is up to date and that Playback support for it is confirmed (see the OS compatibility article). Update Playback from the iOS or Mac App Store.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: iOS performance: clear RAM, force-close all background apps before opening Playback, and do not multitask during a live performance.
USB adapter: an official Apple adapter is required (Lightning to USB3 or USB-C to USB3; both allow simultaneous charging).
USB cable length: max 16 feet for USB 2.0, 3 meters (9 feet) for USB 3.0. Keep the digital USB run short and use longer analog runs (XLR, 1/4") from the interface to DI boxes and the console.
Powered USB extension cables: base cable must respect the limits above; the active repeater needs external power; max extender length 25 m (USB 2.0) or 15 m (USB 3.0).
Powered USB hub: must be powered, no more than 7 USB accessory ports, and only one audio interface connected at a time so Playback sends audio to the correct device.
Auto Pan splitter cable: use a high-quality cable with as few adaptors as possible.
Audio interface: Playback is generally compatible with class-compliant USB interfaces; check the tested supported devices list on multitracks.com.
If issues persist, contact MultiTracks support.

results.title: Why is Playback not sending audio out of my Behringer U-Phoria Audio Interface?
results.summary: Covers the UMC404HD and UMC1820. Multi-output through an interface requires a Pro/Premium subscription. The UMC404HD needs a powered USB hub to be powered properly, and on iPhone/iPad the device's master volume controls the level Playback sends to the interface.

steps.text: Confirm you have the right cables, adapters, and hardware to connect Playback to the interface (see the USB interface connection article).
UMC404HD only: connect through a powered USB hub; the hub powers the interface.
iPhone/iPad: after connecting, turn the iOS device's master volume to maximum, since it directly controls the volume out of Playback into the interface.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > General Settings Tab
results.text:
- Auto-Pan: When enabled, Auto Pan routes the click & guide through the left and all tracks through the right outputs of the iOS device’s stereo output. Auto Pan makes it possible to run tracks from Playback through the headphone output without using an audio interface. Learn about setting up Playback for Auto Pan.
- Click Sound: Choose your favorite Click sound from a variety of built-in Click Track presets. Upload your own custom Click & Guide samples for use in Playback as well.
- Count Into Each Section: Enable to add a 1-bar count-in to every song section marker. Disable to only hear the section cue 1 bar ahead of the marker.
- Song Section Pre-roll: (Playback Premium) Pressing play from the beginning of any section marker will provide a 1-bar count in as well as automatically fade in the tracks. (📖Learn More)
